references.text: The verse describes the fulfillment of the command given in verse 8, where Moses throws dust into the air, causing boils.
Aaron stretches out his staff and dust becomes gnats—a similar action where something is thrown or stretched out to bring about a plague.
The Lord threatens to strike with Egyptian boils—a direct reference to the plague of boils described in this text.
Malignant boils that cannot be healed are mentioned as a curse, referencing the plagues of Egypt.
Job is struck with malignant boils from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head and sits in ashes—similar boils and a connection with dust/ashes.
In Revelation, painful and harmful boils are described as afflicting people—an eschatological parallel to the boils of Egypt.
Direct thematic parallel: Two plagues (dust and gnats) initiated by taking earthly elements and transforming them into judgment upon Egypt.
Thematic parallel: The ritual of stretching out one's hand toward heaven to trigger God's judgment (darkness and hail/dust).
Direct parallel: Both verses describe God's command to stretch out the hand toward heaven to bring a plague (hail/dust) upon Egypt.
